newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma stable over 312, bonds fall, rates up.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma stable over 312, bonds fall, rates up.

text.p: The drachma steadied above 312 against the ecu in late dealings but depos and forex forwards had spiked on concern over the liquidity effect of recent forex outflows and bond prices lost half a point, traders said.

"The drachma is hovering above 312 versus the ecu in late dealings," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "The market is nervous despite the fact that the central bank has shown its willingness to intervene and support the drachma."
The central bank intervened and sold 350 million ecus and 80 million marks for drachmas at today's fixing.
An official at the central bank told Reuters that the monetary and forex policy remained anti-inflationary and recent mild turbulence in ecu/drachma and bonds was largely temporary.
Concerns about tighter interbank liquidity conditions were behind a 30 to 40 basis point rise in depos and a 15 to 50 basis point increase in implied drachma rates from forex forwards, dealers said.
"The forex outflows of the last few days have drained liquidity from the interbank market pulling rates up," said a trader at a private bank.
Bonds had also come under selling with prices losing 30 to 50 basis points, bond traders said.
"Zeros are virtually unchanged but FRNs shed 10 to 15 basis points today and fixed coupon bonds suffered the most shedding about 50 basis points," a bond dealer said.
"There is concern about how much debt paper the ministry will auction but the behaviour of ecu/drachma is at the centre of market attention right now."
The treasury will issue 12-month T-bills at 9.60 percent on June 2, down 10 basis points, reopen bids for three-, five- and seven-year coupon bonds and auction 10-year fixed coupon bonds on June 19.
Greece auctioned three-year, 9.80 percent bonds, five-year, 9.20 percent bonds and seven-year, 8.9 percent bonds on March 19.
The finance ministry cut its three-, six- and 12-month T-bill rates by a tenth of a point to 8.50 percent, 8.80 percent and 9.60 percent respectively effective Monday, it added.
The mark was quoted at 160.10/20 from Monday's 159.870 fix, the dollar at 272.29/39 drachmas from 269.340 and the ecu at 312.12/22 from 311.370 drachmas.

** Overnight at 9.80-10.30

** Two weeks at 9.80-10.30

** Nine months at 9.75-10.25
